revisions.title: From the Forms to the participation dilemma
revisions.body: Here Socrates draws the crucial contrast: sensible participants may display opposite properties, while opposite affections in the Forms themselves would be astonishing. Parmenides then tests the reach of this Forms language—Socrates names likeness, unity, justice, beauty, and goodness, but hesitates over Forms for trivial things. The pressure becomes precise at the end: if particulars participate, do they take the whole Form or only a part?

revisions.title: Participation and training
revisions.body: Parmenides turns participation into a test of explanatory discipline. If a Form is wholly in many things, it separates from itself; if divided, largeness, equality, and smallness produce absurd consequences. Socrates revises the account from Forms as thoughts to Forms as paradigms. I read the closing appeal to training as the method demanded here: define slowly, and follow each definition through its consequences.

revisions.title: The method becomes the subject
revisions.body: I suggest hearing this stretch as a change in method rather than as a verdict about the Forms. Parmenides makes the exercise symmetrical: imagine the subject as existing, then as not existing, and trace what follows through the subject and its relations. On this reading, the passage postpones any final answer about the One; its immediate object is the discipline of following consequences. The next move will make that discipline concrete.

revisions.title: The one that is: a whole with parts
revisions.body: The second hypothesis turns on a grammatical distinction: “the one is” is not “the one is one”; being is added to unity. Once being and unity are distinguished, the existent one becomes a whole with parts. The argument then multiplies the consequences into number and an unlimited multitude of existences. Hear the ending as a test of what a whole requires, not as a claim about shape.

revisions.title: Predicates under pressure
revisions.body: This unit is best heard as a pressure test for descriptions of the One. One way to read it is that containment first unsettles the boundary between self and other, then makes rest and motion, sameness and otherness, likeness and unlikeness, and finally contact depend on how a relation is framed. The dialogue’s point is methodological: a predicate may disclose its contrary when its conditions are made explicit.

revisions.title: Time Turns the One Relational
revisions.body: Here the hypothesis turns time into a stress test for relation. Being is linked to the present, and the One becomes older and younger than itself while also being neither older nor younger, depending on whether we track becoming, the now, or equal duration. From 153a the argument explicitly includes the others: different accounts of generation make the One older, younger, and the same age as them. The point is not a final chronology but the pressure produced when each account is followed consistently.

revisions.title: From the One to the Others
revisions.body: The argument now turns outward. The sequence moves from change at the instant, through the extension of that pattern across contrary transitions, to the claim that the Others form a whole with parts and so participate in the One. One way to hear the shift in method is that the exercise begins mapping the structure of what is other.

revisions.title: A stricter second pass
revisions.body: I read the turn at 163b–164c as a stress test of the negation. The dialogue first lets the hypothesis produce a contradiction, then restarts by taking “is not” without qualification. For me, that restart is the point: it narrows the terms before the argument proceeds, shifting attention from what the non-existent One can undergo to what follows when participation in being is denied altogether. The passage therefore tests a rule of reasoning, not simply a definition of non-being.

revisions.title: When unity disappears, predicates collapse
revisions.body: One way to hear this stretch is as a test of what “the others” can mean when unity is unavailable. The argument first multiplies every apparent unit, then withdraws even the appearances of number, likeness, relation, and motion. Its force is not a description of objects so much as a demonstration that ordinary predicates depend upon the One. The closing reversal leaves the exercise suspended between affirmation and denial.
